title: stormwatch-lane-transitions
content:
Summary:
This is a lightweight, personal on-call handoff quickplay for the night lane (\"Stormwatch\"). Purpose: preserve context, surface active problems, and list immediate steps for continuity. Not polished — treat as working scratchpad; canonical runbooks live in Confluence but are sometimes too slow during incidents.

Quick status (at handoff):
- Active incidents: 0 (no P1s).
- Noise: Frequent spike alerts from embedding-cache on pool-3 (see noise section).
- Ongoing work: Diego is running a canary that toggles KV cache TTLs for small-history workloads (canary-id: canary-cache-ttl-7). Expect transient 202 responses while the canary rolls.
- Important reminders: Dedicated pool redwood-dedicated-europe has reduced capacity after maintenance window; if routing falls back, latency will increase ~60–120ms.

Pre-handoff checklist (what I did & what to check next):
1) Confirm health endpoints for each serving tier:
   - Hosted API: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/healthz | jq .
   - Dedicated pool: curl -sS https://10.2.3.14:8443/healthz -k (via VPN)
   - Private: check the customer VPN circuit and /metrics on rule-agent container.
2) Open consoles: Grafana (latency-dashboard -> lane=stormwatch), Sentry (filter: lane=stormwatch), PagerDuty (oncall schedule).
3) Tail last 30m logs for model fallback events:
   - s3://redwood-logs/lane-stormwatch/2026-03-09/*.gz (use aws s3 cp + zcat or the archive viewer)
4) Leave a sticky note on Slack channel #ops-night with summary + personal mobile contact.

Triage play (fast path):
- If 5xx spike on hosted-api route:
  1. Check \"error-type\" tags in logs (model-binding, kv-cache, runtimeOOM).
  2. Hit the model health endpoint directly (bypass load balancer): curl --connect-timeout 2 -sS http://10.x.y.z:8080/model/status
  3. If runtimeOOM or kernel error: scale down batch size on that node pool (kubectl patch HPA...) and notify serving-runtime on-call.
  4. If kv-cache misses spike: re-enable fallback-cache (temp) by flipping feature flag: /admin/feature-flip fallback-kv:true
- If latency increases (p95 > 800ms):
  1. Check redis/kv cache hit rate in Grafana (panel: kv-hit-rate -> lane=stormwatch).
  2. If hit-rate < 65%: route critical customers to dedicated pools (manual override in routing UI -> set policy lane=critical -> pool=dedicated-temp-1).
  3. If model tokenization CPU bound: reduce max_tokens client-side via routing rate limit.

Known noisy alerts (mute suggestions):
- ALERT: embedding-cache:pool-3: transient-err (noisy between 02:00-03:15 UTC historically). Suggest an auto-mute rule for 02:00-03:30 UTC for non-P0 alerts.
- ALERT: k8s-node-disk-pressure on infra-node-5 (flaps every few hours, tracked in JIRA). It's safe to suppress non-critical drains during night unless eviction rate > 0.5%.

Escalation matrix (who to ping):
- First: on-call SRE (channel @ops-night, PD escalation).
- Second: Diego Alvarez (serving runtime lead) — for kernel/runtime issues.
- Third: Priya Raman (platform infra) — for routing / autoscaler issues.
- Fourth: Eng leadership paging only if incident is >30m and impacting >10% of traffic.

Short command cheat-sheet (copy/paste safe):
- Health check hosted: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/healthz | jq .
- Direct model probe: curl -m 2 http://10.33.120.7:8080/model/status || echo \"model probe failed\"
- Toggle fallback cache (admin): curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' https://admin.redwood.ai/feature-flip -d '{"fallback-kv":true}'
- Tail recent logs: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/lane-stormwatch/2026-03-09/part-000.gz - | zcat | jq -r '.message' | tail -n 200
- Quick rollback (model): aws ssm send-command --document-name \"RunShellScript\" --targets Key=tag:Name,Values=model-hosts --parameters commands=['/opt/release/rollback.sh v1.12.3']

Temporary mitigations (if you need to stabilize quickly):
- Short-term: Enable model-fallback policy to smaller-quant model for high-latency routes. Reduces quality but restores latency.
- Mid-term: Increase kserving replicas for heavy pipelines (watch CPU and KV miss).
- For persistent 5xx from a pool: move traffic to hosted-api-offload (route -> policy: cost-tier=offload).

Post-incident notes (what to capture):
- Time window of degradation, snapshot links (Grafana), top error traces (Sentry ids), exact routing decisions made, any feature flags toggled, and whether rollback was executed.
- Add postmortem stub in Confluence under Support -> Night Lane -> {date} with commands run + raw logs link.

Unresolved/To-do: 
- Decide whether to keep the embedding-cache auto-mute (file a quick RFC in #infra-proposals).
- Follow up on dedicated-europe capacity: Priya to confirm completion of maintenance and new headroom numbers.
- Add a short model-probe endpoint that performs a sample generation and returns p50/p95 (ticket: JIRA-OPS-612).

Notes to next person taking lane:
- If you see repeated fallback-cache toggles in the audit log (more than 3 times in 1h) — escalate to Diego immediately.
- Trust the route -> pool override for critical customers; it won’t persist beyond the window if you uncheck \"sticky\" in the routing console.
- I leave a small sticky with my cellphone in #ops-night pinned messages if you need a quick hand.

Random tips and heuristics I rely on:
- When p95 jumps but errors do not: think caching/queueing first, not models.
- Cold KV cache fills are explosive — if you must rewarm, do it with a sampled prefix, not full dataset.
- If you flip a flag, always capture the admin API response (it has a UUID you want in postmortem).

Slack summary to paste (1-liner):
\"Stormwatch: no open P1s. Watch embedding-cache pool-3 noise; Diego running TTL canary. Dedicated-eu capacity reduced post-maintenance; expect higher latency for some customers. Ping @ops-night for triage\"

End of doc.

(Old drafts: I sometimes keep a checklist of 'first 10 minutes' vs 'next 30 minutes' — willing to add that if useful.)
